issues.what: A pre-study 'timing benchmark on one chronological IS split' looked at IS AUC vs alpha and led to re-parametrising the L2 grid as a per-sample penalty (C = 1/(alpha n), i.e. ~3,300x stronger regularisation than sklearn's C = 1/alpha reading of 1e-3..1e3). This is an IS look outside the ledger and outside the nested CV; it is disclosed in the docstring but not listed in findings.json caveats as such.
issues.evidence: Docstring: 'A timing benchmark on one chronological IS split before the study ran, no ledger row, showed that with sklearn's unnormalised C the optimum sat on the grid's edge ... the per-sample convention was adopted for that reason'. Chosen alphas (results.json cpcv.alpha_rocket_counts: 57/66 at 10.0) sit inside the shifted grid. Direction of effect: a better-regularised probe raises rocket/stacked AUC, i.e. works against the stop, so the null result is conservative with respect to this look.
issues.fix: State it in findings.json caveats as an un-ledgered IS look that can only have favoured the probe; nothing to rerun.

issues.what: Judge 1's pre-registered stop form ('stacked - tabular AUC < 0.02 in every fold') is NOT met on this data (block 10 gain +0.0516), so under Judge 1's rule alone the study would have continued to distillation; the study made Judge 2's CPCV-p5 rule the operative stop and reports Judge 1's form only as a footnote, without saying the two rules disagree here.
issues.evidence: Recomputed per-block stacked-tabular gains from oof_scores.npz: [0.0132, -0.0204, -0.0183, 0.0076, 0.0063, 0.0072, -0.0026, 0.0040, -0.0051, 0.0037, 0.0516, -0.0084]; all < 0.02 = False. CPCV p5 = -0.0073 < 0.03 -> Judge 2 stop fires. The choice of Judge 2's rule as the operative stop was fixed in the docstring before the run and is the stricter of the two; with no candidate slot, distillation could only have added ledger rows.
issues.fix: One sentence in FINDINGS §4: the two judges' stop forms disagree on this data; Judge 2's (pre-registered as operative, stricter) governs; distillation would have produced no candidate in any case.

issues.what: The docstring claim 'OOS features are never read' holds for the window tensor but not for the 244-column base design: harness.design(T) enumerates one-hot levels (and applies the 16-level cap) over all rows including OOS, so OOS feature values (never labels) shape the column set. This is a harness-wide property used by every study, not specific to this one.

issues.what: The inner GroupKFold used for alpha choice and for the training-fold threshold OOF groups by harness block but applies no 3-session embargo between inner train and inner test blocks (only the outer splitter is purged/embargoed). Because the L1 label is intraday and blocks are whole sessions, no label lifetime crosses an inner boundary; the only effect is on alpha/threshold selection, never on the test-fold scores.
issues.evidence: GroupKFold(n_splits=5).split(..., groups=T.block[tr]); no call to _purge or block_embargo inside. Harness Table: exit_bar = l1_exit_i (same session as entry by definition of L1), so entry..exit never spans two blocks.
issues.fix: Note it in FINDINGS §11; optionally purge the inner folds with the harness's embargo in any future rerun. Not material for the null result.
